description: Among the questions asked, President Trump indicated that he "knew nothing" about Epstein's victims, emphasizing that "Jeffrey Epstein and I had a very bad relationship for many years." He further stated that he hadn't considered a Presidential pardon for Maxwell. When asked about Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene's previous interview with CBS stating that all the files should be released, he responded back saying, "they can have whatever [files] they want..." I was never on his island. Bill Clinton went there supposedly 28 times. He further said that if there was anything incriminating on him, that Democratic leaders would have used it against him in the election. When asked why his team asked Reps. Nancy Mace and Lauren Boebert to not pursue the Epstein files, he responded by saying that "it's bad to talk about it" when Republicans should be talking about "how well we've done."
headline: President Trump Answers Reporter Questions about Epstein and Maxwell on Air Force 1

info.description: President Trump silenced a reporter question in the gaggle about the Epstein files, calling her "piggy".
info.note: Bloomsberg reporter Catherine Lucey questioned why, 'if there was nothing incriminating in the files, why he was acting like there is,' to which Trump pointed directly at her and responded, "Quiet. Quiet, piggy."

info.description: 2025-11-20: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt responded to President Trump's "piggy" remarks.
info.note: She stated that Trump sometimes "gets frustrated with reporters," calling him "a lot more respectful" than previous President Joe Biden, and that he "is very frank and honest with everyone in the room."

description: The House this day passed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, a bill that would require the Department of Justice to release previously sealed documents related to Jeffrey Epstein's criminal cases within 90 days of enactment, barring certain exceptions for privacy and ongoing investigations. This bill was orginally presented for consideration by co-authors Reps. Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie.
headline: U.S. House Passes Epstein Files Transparency Act

info.description: The House passed the act 427-1, with Rep. Clay Higgins (R-LA) being the sole vote against it, sending the bill to the Senate for consideration.
info.note: The bill now passes to the Senate.

info.description: Rep. Higgins stated in a press release that he voted against the bill because it "...reveals and injures thousands of innocent people –[sic] witnesses, people who provided alibis, family members, etc."
Rep. Donald Beyer [D-VA], Rep. Greg Casar [D-TX], Rep. Michael A. Rulli [R-OH], Rep. Mikie Sherill [D-NJ], and Rep. Steve Womack [R-AR] were not present for the vote.
info.note: All save Rep. Rulli indicated current or previous support for the bill, had they been present.
